caption: N=1 baseline: a lever on the back of a sticky piston.

N=2, slime + observer, flat, 7 blocks: A pushes a slime row (S1 under B, S2 under the payload, S3 under its +1 spot); the observer hangs under S1 and powers it (B stands on it; A ignores its own front) 2 gt after every landing. Out: B spits the payload one more cell. Back: the frame drags the payload back one cell, B's landing pulse reach-pulls it home.
N=2, slime + observer, 7 blocks: the observer beside S1 powers it (B stands on it).

N=2, slime-free, 7 blocks: an observer watching the input gives a 2 gt pulse on BOTH edges to A (through the stone beside it) and to a second sticky piston that carries an observer. On: A pushes B + payload and spits them (B lands next to the input, which holds it extended: the payload goes one more cell). Off: B retracts (payload back one), A's pulse reach-pulls B home, and the carried observer, pulled home too, fires on landing into B (variant 1: where it sits), whose 2 gt pulse reach-pulls the payload home. The lever hangs on the input observer.

N=3 rider (minimized from n3-rider-v1 by mctas circuit pext minimize): A (lever on its back) pushes a 5-slime row carrying B, C and the payload; one observer under the frame fires C first after each landing, then the input-driven chain (a sticky piston + observers, a lamp, a dust run) fires B and C again: inner train C B C on both edges.

N=3 rider, fully wired (first working version, not minimized). A (lever on its back) pushes a 5-slime row carrying B, C and the payload (latched at their extended spots). After each landing the inner train C B C: C1 = two observers hanging under the frame (landing burst into S1/S2); B = observer chain from the lever (P2 pulses x=2 at t12, P3 x=3 at t14); C2 = the chain climbs (V1, a dust line, Z) to X5 (pulses x=5 at t18) and U (2 gt later, through a stone into x=3).

N=2, GRAVITY (sand payload), travel up: an observer under the lever pulses A (through the stone beside it) on both edges. On: A spits B + sand up one cell; B lands next to the lever, which holds it extended (sand up one more). Off: B retracts and the sand falls onto it; A's pulse reach-pulls B back down and the sand falls home on top of it.

N=2, GRAVITY (sand payload), travel up, ONE BUTTON PRESS (stone): an observer under the button pulses A (through the stone beside it) on the press and on the release. Press: A spits B + sand up one cell; B lands next to the button, which holds it extended (sand up one more). Release: B retracts and the sand falls onto it; A's pulse reach-pulls B back down and the sand falls home.

N=2, slime-free, FLAT (1 wide), 8 blocks: sf7 folded into one plane. The lever hangs above B's final cell; the observer beside it pulses A through the stone on A's top (both edges) and, through A's cell, the sticky piston under A that carries the observer under B.

N=3 CASCADE extender, minimized from n3-cascade-v1 (mctas circuit pext minimize): units [slime + sticky piston + observer under the slime] in a line; a moved unit fires its own piston 2 gt after landing, so only the round starts come from the lever (C, then B, then A). The minimizer replaced observer runs of the timing chain by pistons used as delays.

N=3 CASCADE extender (wired): units [slime + sticky piston + observer under the slime] in a line (A, unit B, unit C, payload). A unit that is moved fires its own piston 2 gt after landing, so the pulse-toggle train C B C A B C needs only the three round starts from outside, all from the lever: C at t4 (pulsers above-beside x5 and x7, quasi-connectivity), B at t12 (x3) then t14 (x4), A at t26 (observer on A's top). Pulsers sit diagonal to the slime cells so no slime ever drags them.
